healthBenefits: Ophthalmological Protection: High beta-carotene and zeaxanthin content protect the retina from damage caused by light exposure.
Cardio-metabolic Support: Adenosine and potassium work synergistically to improve coronary blood flow and control blood pressure.
Skin Regeneration: High levels of vitamin C and antioxidants stimulate epithelial tissue renewal and improve skin turgor.
Detoxification and Hydration: Possesses a mild diuretic effect, promoting the cleansing of urinary tracts and maintaining overall fluid levels in the body.
melon.precautionsIntro: Melon is an active enzymatic product that requires careful attention regarding how it is consumed:
precautions: GI Fermentation: Consuming melon immediately after a heavy protein or fatty meal often leads to excessive fermentation, causing bloating and heaviness. It is recommended to consume it as a separate meal.
Glycemic Risk: Contains easily digestible sugars; individuals with diabetes should strictly dose consumption to avoid glycemic spikes.
Nitrate Load: Like other gourd crops, melons are prone to accumulating nitrogen fertilizers in the rind. It is necessary to clean the pulp thoroughly, avoiding the area near the rind.
Individual Sensitivity: High sugar content can exacerbate conditions associated with Small Intestinal Bacterial Overgrowth (SIBO).

cucumber.name: Cucumber
cucumber.description: Cucumber is a highly hydrating vegetable matrix possessing low energy density and a high concentration of electrolytes. It serves as a fundamental tool for maintaining systemic water balance and detoxifying the body, providing a supply of phytochemical compounds (cucurbitacins) that possess anti-inflammatory and protective potential.
cucumber.macroTitle: Macro Nutrients (per 100g, raw product with peel)
cucumber.macroIntro: The macronutrient composition of cucumber is almost entirely focused on supporting hydration, making it an indispensable component of metabolic weight loss protocols.
cucumber.microIntro: The product is a unique source of organic silica and specific polyphenols that act synergistically on the integrity of connective tissue and the antioxidant defense of cells.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Extremely low energy value with significant volume, providing a quick feeling of satiety.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Contains trace amounts of amino acids, having no significant nutritional load.

macroNutrients.name: Fat
macroNutrients.description: Virtually zero lipids, supporting the dietary lightness of the product.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Represented primarily by non-digestible fiber, supporting intestinal peristalsis.

microNutrients.name: Cucurbitacins
microNutrients.description: Specific compounds possessing marked anti-tumor and anti-inflammatory effects.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin K
microNutrients.description: Necessary for bone mineralization processes and blood clotting regulation.

microNutrients.name: Potassium
microNutrients.description: A key intracellular electrolyte, normalizing fluid balance and vascular system function.

microNutrients.name: Silica
microNutrients.description: An element contributing to the strengthening of collagen fibers, improving the condition of skin, hair, and nails.

microNutrients.name: Lignans
microNutrients.description: Phytoestrogens that reduce the risk of hormone-dependent pathologies and improve antioxidant status.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin C
microNutrients.description: Supports local immunity and neutralizes free radicals.

healthBenefits: Hydration Optimization: Cucumber's structured water has high bioavailability, contributing to the efficient excretion of metabolic waste products.
Connective Tissue Support: High silica content strengthens structural proteins, promoting skin elasticity and the durability of bone structures.
Glycemic Profile Regulation: Due to its low glycemic index and fiber content, cucumber does not trigger an insulin response.
Anti-inflammatory Activity: Cucurbitacins and flavonoids systemically reduce markers of inflammation, protecting cells from premature aging.
cucumber.precautionsIntro: Cucumber is considered a safe product; however, to prevent side effects, consumption specifics should be considered:
precautions: Nitrate Profile: Early-season and greenhouse cucumbers are prone to nitrate accumulation, especially in the peel and near the stem. Peeling is recommended if the origin is uncertain.
Bloating in IBS: In individuals with Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) or flatulence, consuming raw cucumbers may provoke discomfort due to the high fiber content and specific sugars.
Anti-nutrient Components: The presence of cucurbitacins in some varieties may impart bitterness and, in excess, cause mild gastric mucosal irritation.
Compatibility: Due to enzymatic activity, cucumbers are not always recommended to be mixed with dairy products, as this may provoke digestive disturbances in individuals with sensitive GI tracts.

kefir.name: Kefir
kefir.description: Kefir is a highly effective fermented probiotic matrix obtained by fermenting milk with kefir grains. It represents a complex symbiosis of beneficial bacteria and yeasts, possessing a marked modulating effect on the intestinal microbiota and the body's systemic immune reactivity.
kefir.macroIntro: The macronutrient profile of kefir is balanced to provide the body with easily digestible proteins and a moderate amount of dairy fats, which contributes to high-quality tissue regeneration.
kefir.microIntro: Kefir is a unique carrier of metabolically active compounds, B-vitamins, and organic acids, working synergistically to support the body's internal environment.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Moderate energy density, providing complete nutritional intake at a controlled calorie level.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Easily digestible dairy protein (casein and whey proteins) containing the full spectrum of essential amino acids.

macroNutrients.name: Fat
macroNutrients.description: Dairy fats in emulsified form, necessary for the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Represented by lactose, which is partially fermented during the maturation process, making the product easier to digest.

microNutrients.name: Probiotic Cultures
microNutrients.description: A unique complex of lactobacilli, bifidobacteria, and beneficial yeasts colonizing the gut.

microNutrients.name: Calcium
microNutrients.description: An essential mineral for the structural integrity of bone tissue and the transmission of nerve impulses.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B12
microNutrients.description: Critically important for hematopoiesis and neuronal metabolism.

microNutrients.name: Phosphorus
microNutrients.description: Supports energy metabolism (ATP) and skeletal system health.

microNutrients.name: Riboflavin (B2)
microNutrients.description: Participates in oxidation-reduction reaction processes and vision maintenance.

microNutrients.name: Organic Acids
microNutrients.description: Lactic and acetic acids, creating an optimal pH environment in the gut.

healthBenefits: Microbiome Correction: Kefir is one of the most powerful natural sources of probiotics that restore the diversity of intestinal flora.
Immune Modulation: Through its impact on the GALT system (gut-associated lymphoid tissue), systematic consumption of kefir increases the body's overall resistance.
GI Optimization: Organic acids and enzymes contribute to efficient food digestion and regular bowel motility.
Metabolic Improvement: Regular consumption contributes to improving the cholesterol profile and stabilizing blood sugar levels.
kefir.precautionsIntro: Kefir is a biologically active product, so it is important to consider individual characteristics when including it in the diet:
precautions: Lactose Intolerance: Despite partial lactose breakdown, people with severe lactase deficiency may experience symptoms of indigestion.
Acidity: High organic acid content may cause discomfort in individuals with hyperacidic gastritis or peptic ulcers in the acute stage.
Alcohol Content: Natural kefir contains trace amounts of ethanol (a result of yeast fermentation). This amount is minimal, but should be considered if strictly abstaining.
Product Freshness: Kefir has different effects on the GI tract depending on storage time: fresh (one-day) has a mild laxative effect, while 'old' (three-day) has a constipating effect.

cheese.name: Cheese
cheese.description: Cheese is a highly concentrated protein-lipid matrix obtained through the fermentation and coagulation of milk protein. It is a nutritionally dense product that serves as a rich source of bioavailable calcium, complete animal protein, and fat-soluble vitamins, providing structural support for the skeletal system and metabolic processes.
cheese.macroTitle: Macro Nutrients (per 100g, average values for semi-hard varieties)
cheese.macroIntro: Cheese is characterized by high energy density and an optimal ratio of macronutrients, making it a strategic product for maintaining muscle tone and energy balance.
cheese.microIntro: The product is a unique storehouse of essential nutrients, including vitamins A, D, and B12, and mineral elements that work synergistically to maintain physiological homeostasis.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: High energy capacity, ensuring prolonged satiety and high performance.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: A concentrated source of casein, providing the body with the necessary set of amino acids for tissue regeneration.

macroNutrients.name: Fat
macroNutrients.description: Animal-based fats, necessary for hormone synthesis and the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Minimal carbohydrate content due to the almost complete fermentation of lactose during the maturation process.

microNutrients.name: Calcium
microNutrients.description: The most bioavailable form of the mineral, critically important for skeletal health and muscle contraction.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin A
microNutrients.description: Supports the regeneration of mucous membranes, immune defense, and visual function.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B12
microNutrients.description: Essential for DNA synthesis, hematopoiesis, and the metabolic health of the nervous system.

microNutrients.name: Phosphorus
microNutrients.description: Together with calcium, it forms the mineral basis of the skeleton and participates in energy metabolism (ATP).

microNutrients.name: Zinc
microNutrients.description: A mineral involved in protein synthesis and supporting the body's defense mechanisms.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin K2
microNutrients.description: Regulates calcium transport, preventing its deposition in blood vessels and directing it into bone tissue.

healthBenefits: Skeletal Support: The unique combination of calcium, phosphorus, and vitamin K2 provides fundamental strength to bone structures.
Protein Synthesis: The high concentration of casein makes cheese an effective product for maintaining muscle mass and long-term metabolic satiety.
Oral Health: Regular cheese consumption helps increase the oral cavity's pH, reducing tooth enamel demineralization.
Neuroendocrine Stability: Cheese fats and amino acids contribute to maintaining hormonal balance and cognitive functions.
cheese.precautionsIntro: Cheese is a highly active product, so it should be included in the diet considering the following aspects:
precautions: Sodium Content: Hard and aged varieties often contain high doses of salt, which requires monitoring in cases of arterial hypertension or kidney disease.
Saturated Fats: The high content of saturated fatty acids requires portion limitation for individuals with dyslipidemia and a tendency toward cardiovascular pathologies.
Amines and Histamine: Aged cheeses contain tyramine and other biogenic amines that may provoke headaches in sensitive individuals.
Individual Intolerance: Despite the low lactose content, allergy to dairy proteins (casein) is a direct contraindication for consuming most types of cheese.

lemon.name: Lemon
lemon.description: Lemon is a highly concentrated biochemical agent belonging to the Rutaceae family. It is valued for its unique content of citric acid, high doses of ascorbic acid, and a wide spectrum of phytonutrients (flavonoids), which provide powerful antioxidant protection and optimization of metabolic processes in the body.
lemon.macroIntro: Lemon is characterized by extremely low caloric content and an almost total absence of fat and protein, making it a tool for flavor and nutritional modulation of dishes without significantly changing their energy density.
lemon.microIntro: The product is a complex storehouse of vitamins and organic compounds, playing a critical role in maintaining immune status and systemic detoxification.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Minimal energy footprint, allowing the product to be used without restricting caloric intake.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Contains a negligible amount of plant-based proteins.

macroNutrients.name: Fat
macroNutrients.description: Virtually zero lipids.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Represented by simple sugars and organic acids, contributing to improved digestion.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin C
microNutrients.description: A powerful antioxidant, critically important for collagen synthesis and immune defense.

microNutrients.name: Citric Acid
microNutrients.description: An organic acid that promotes improved digestion and helps prevent kidney stone formation.

microNutrients.name: Flavonoids
microNutrients.description: Hesperidin and eriocitrin—compounds protecting cells from oxidative damage.

microNutrients.name: Potassium
microNutrients.description: Important for maintaining electrolyte balance and regulating blood pressure.

microNutrients.name: Folate (B9)
microNutrients.description: Necessary for cell division and tissue renewal processes.

microNutrients.name: Limonene
microNutrients.description: An aromatic compound with marked anti-inflammatory and anti-tumor potential.

healthBenefits: Immune Stimulation: High concentration of Vitamin C activates the phagocytic activity of immune system cells.
Cardiovascular Support: Flavonoids and potassium contribute to reducing systemic vascular inflammation and normalizing blood pressure.
Renal Prophylaxis: Citric acid increases urinary citrate levels, which inhibits the crystallization of oxalate stones.
Metabolic Activation: Consuming lemon water promotes the stimulation of digestive enzyme secretion.
lemon.precautionsIntro: Despite the benefits, the high acidity of lemon requires caution in the following conditions:
precautions: GERD: High acidity may provoke heartburn and esophageal mucosal irritation in individuals with GERD.
Enamel Erosion: Direct contact of lemon juice with teeth demineralizes the enamel. Using a straw or rinsing the mouth with water is recommended.
Ulcerative Lesions: In cases of gastritis or stomach ulcer exacerbation, lemon juice consumption is strictly not recommended due to the risk of mucosal damage.
Allergic Reactions: Citrus fruits are known allergens. Individuals with hypersensitivity should exercise caution when introducing them for the first time.

peaches.name: Peaches
peaches.description: The peach is a highly functional fruit, representing a concentrated matrix of organic acids, soluble fibers, and carotenoid pigments. It is an effective metabolic modulator that supports the health of epithelial tissues, immune function, and the body's optimal antioxidant balance.
peaches.macroIntro: The macronutrient composition of the peach is characterized by moderate energy density and high sugar availability, ensuring the rapid restoration of glycogen stores during physical activity.
peaches.microIntro: Peaches are a unique source of polyphenolic compounds that work synergistically to reduce systemic inflammation and protect cellular structures from oxidative damage.

macroNutrients.description: Moderate energy value combined with high nutritional density.

macroNutrients.name: Protein

macroNutrients.description: Minimal lipid content, contributing to the easy digestibility of the product.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Represented by fructose and glucose, which provide a gentle yet rapid influx of energy.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin C
microNutrients.description: Critically important for collagen synthesis and strengthening the body's defenses.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin A (beta-carotene)
microNutrients.description: An antioxidant necessary for retinal health and maintaining skin integrity.

microNutrients.name: Potassium
microNutrients.description: An electrolyte involved in regulating blood pressure and smooth muscle contraction.

microNutrients.name: Niacin (B3)
microNutrients.description: Participates in cellular respiration and energy metabolism processes.

microNutrients.name: Dietary Fiber
microNutrients.description: Ensures normal GI tract motility and the maintenance of a healthy microbiota.

microNutrients.name: Chlorogenic Acid
microNutrients.description: A phenolic compound contributing to antioxidant protection and glucose metabolism modulation.

healthBenefits: Dermatological Support: The high concentration of vitamins and antioxidants contributes to improved skin turgor and protection against UV-induced damage.
Cardioprotection: Regular consumption of peaches contributes to the normalization of blood lipid profiles and the reduction of systemic inflammation.
Digestive Modulation: Soluble fibers promote smooth food transit and prevent digestive disturbances.
Antioxidant Status: Phenolic compounds and carotenoids neutralize free radicals, slowing down cellular aging processes.
peaches.precautionsIntro: Peaches are a safe product, but their consumption should take into account physiological characteristics:
precautions: Allergic Reactions: Due to the presence of specific lipid-transfer proteins (LTP), peaches can cause food allergies, especially in individuals with pollinosis (pollen allergy).
Glycemic Profile: Although the fruit has a moderate glycemic index, individuals with diabetes should limit the consumption of very sweet varieties.
Dyspepsia: In people with Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) or fructose intolerance, consuming large amounts of peaches can provoke fermentation and gas.
Nitrate Load: Like other fruits, peaches can accumulate fertilizers if agricultural protocols are violated, so thorough washing of the fruits is recommended.

dill.name: Dill
dill.description: Dill is a biologically active phytomatrix possessing pronounced antispasmodic, carminative, and antibacterial potential. It is a concentrate of essential oils (notably carvone and limonene), which modulate digestive tract functions and support the systemic antioxidant status of the organism.
dill.macroIntro: Dill is a low-calorie product with an extremely low density of macronutrients, making it a valuable functional addition to the diet without significantly altering energy balance.
dill.microIntro: The product is a unique source of phytonutrients and trace elements working synergistically to normalize metabolism and support immune system health.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Low energy value with high concentration of active phyto-compounds.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Contains plant-based proteins that contribute to the overall nutritional enrichment of the diet.

macroNutrients.name: Fat
macroNutrients.description: Minimal lipid content, mainly represented by essential oil components.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Represented primarily by dietary fibers that improve intestinal peristalsis.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin C
microNutrients.description: High concentration of antioxidant for cell protection and immune function stimulation.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin A (beta-carotene)
microNutrients.description: Essential nutrient for mucosal health and visual acuity.

microNutrients.name: Calcium
microNutrients.description: Critically important for bone mineralization and nerve conduction.

microNutrients.name: Iron
microNutrients.description: Necessary for hematopoiesis processes and oxygen delivery to tissues.

microNutrients.name: Manganese
microNutrients.description: Mineral involved in antioxidant defense and connective tissue metabolism.

microNutrients.name: Carvone and Limonene
microNutrients.description: Essential oils providing antispasmodic and antimicrobial effects.

healthBenefits: Digestive Modulation: Dill effectively relaxes the smooth muscles of the intestines, eliminating spasms, bloating, and flatulence.
Antimicrobial Activity: The phytoncides contained in the plant suppress pathogenic flora, contributing to the improvement of the intestinal environment.
Metabolic Support: High content of vitamins and minerals strengthens the body's protective barrier and contributes to general recovery.
Cardiovascular Regulation: Dill flavonoids contribute to blood pressure stabilization and the reduction of systemic inflammation.
dill.precautionsIntro: Dill is safe when used in culinary doses, but requires consideration of some nuances:
precautions: Photosensitivity: When taking concentrated dill extracts, increased skin sensitivity to ultraviolet light (photosensitization) is possible.
Hypotension: Excessive consumption of dill can lead to an excessive decrease in blood pressure, which is important for individuals prone to hypotension.
Allergic Reactions: In individuals sensitive to plants of the Apiaceae family, dill consumption may provoke allergic reactions.
Pregnancy: In pharmacological doses, dill extracts are not recommended during pregnancy due to potential effects on uterine tone.

parsley.name: Parsley
parsley.description: Parsley is a nutritionally dense phytomatrix possessing powerful diuretic and anti-inflammatory potential. It serves as a unique source of vitamins C, K, and specific flavonoids (apigenin), which exert a protective effect on the vascular wall and support the body's antioxidant homeostasis.
parsley.macroIntro: Parsley is characterized by low energy density with a significant content of bioactive compounds, making it an ideal component for the functional enrichment of any diet.
parsley.microIntro: The plant is a biochemical concentrate of essential nutrients that contribute to the detoxification of the body and the improvement of the metabolic profile.

macroNutrients.description: Low-calorie product with a high concentration of protective phytonutrients.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Contains plant-based protein, complementing the amino acid composition of the diet.

macroNutrients.name: Fat

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Contains dietary fibers that optimize intestinal peristalsis.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin K
microNutrients.description: Extremely high concentration for blood clotting and bone metabolism.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin C
microNutrients.description: Powerful antioxidant for immune support and collagen synthesis.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin A (beta-carotene)
microNutrients.description: Important for vision health, mucosal membranes, and the immune system.

microNutrients.name: Iron
microNutrients.description: Critically important for hemoglobin synthesis and energy metabolism.

microNutrients.name: Apigenin
microNutrients.description: Flavonoid with anti-tumor and anxiolytic potential.

microNutrients.name: Potassium
microNutrients.description: Electrolyte supporting vascular tone and water balance.

healthBenefits: Cardiovascular Protection: Apigenin and folic acid contribute to lowering homocysteine levels and improving arterial elasticity.
Diuretic Effect: Myristicin and apiol contained in parsley oil stimulate kidney function, facilitating the excretion of excess fluid.
Bone Mineralization: An extremely high concentration of Vitamin K ensures correct calcium fixation in bone tissue.
Antioxidant Support: High levels of vitamins C and A systemically suppress free radical activity.
parsley.precautionsIntro: Parsley is a product with pronounced biological activity, so the following should be considered:
precautions: Pregnancy: In concentrated forms (essential oils), parsley may stimulate uterine contractions, so it should be avoided in therapeutic doses.
Kidney Disease: Due to high oxalate content, regular consumption of very large doses of greens requires caution if prone to kidney stones.
Interaction with Anticoagulants: High levels of Vitamin K may reduce the effectiveness of blood-thinning medications (e.g., warfarin).
Allergy: Individual hypersensitivity to plants of the Apiaceae family is possible.

apricot.name: Apricot
apricot.description: The apricot is a functional fruit that serves as a concentrated source of carotenoids and potassium. It is an effective metabolic agent that promotes optimization of the cardiovascular system, improves tissue regeneration, and supports the body's antioxidant homeostasis.
apricot.macroIntro: Apricots have moderate energy density and high fiber content, ensuring stable energy release and normalization of digestive tract function.
apricot.microIntro: The fruit is a unique biochemical storehouse of vitamins A, C, and E, working synergistically to protect cells from oxidative damage.

healthBenefits: Cardio-metabolic Support: High potassium levels contribute to blood pressure stabilization and maintenance of myocardial health.
Ophthalmological Protection: Carotenoids (beta-carotene, zeaxanthin) protect the retina from degenerative changes.
Digestive Optimization: Fiber improves peristalsis, preventing constipation and supporting gut microbiota.
Tissue Regeneration: The combination of vitamins A, C, and E accelerates the healing of epithelial structures.
apricot.precautionsIntro: Apricots are beneficial, but their consumption has physiological limitations:
precautions: Sugar Content: In dried form, sugar concentration is extremely high, requiring monitoring in cases of diabetes.
Acidity: Large quantities of consumed fresh apricots can provoke a laxative effect and discomfort in people with sensitive GI tracts.
Pits: The kernels of the pits contain amygdalin, which releases cyanide during metabolism. Consuming large amounts of kernels is dangerous.
Allergy: Individual intolerance is possible, especially in individuals sensitive to birch pollen or other stone fruits.

whole-wheat-bread.name: Whole Wheat Bread
whole-wheat-bread.description: Whole wheat bread is a high-energy matrix of complex carbohydrates obtained from flour containing all parts of the grain (bran, endosperm, and germ). It is a fundamental source of slowly released glucose, dietary fiber, and a wide spectrum of micronutrients necessary for maintaining metabolic stability and GI tract health.
whole-wheat-bread.macroIntro: The macronutrient profile of the product is balanced to provide prolonged satiety, preventing sharp insulin spikes in the systemic bloodstream.
whole-wheat-bread.microIntro: The bread serves as a carrier for key B-vitamins and minerals that play a critical role in nervous system functioning and energy metabolism.

healthBenefits: Glycemic Stabilization: A low glycemic index helps prevent metabolic crashes and maintains stable blood sugar levels.
Intestinal Support: Fiber stimulates peristalsis and creates an environment for the proliferation of beneficial microflora.
Cardiovascular Support: Regular consumption of whole grains is associated with a lower risk of hypertension and CHD.
Satiety and Weight Control: High fiber content ensures rapid satiety, helping to control the volume of consumed calories.
whole-wheat-bread.precautionsIntro: Despite its high nutritional value, whole wheat bread requires consideration of some aspects:
precautions: Gluten Sensitivity: For individuals with celiac disease or gluten intolerance, consumption of this product is strictly contraindicated.
Anti-nutrients: Whole grains contain phytic acid, which can reduce the bioavailability of certain minerals (zinc, calcium) if consumed in excess.
GI Irritation: In individuals with acute gastritis or irritable bowel syndrome, rough fibers can cause mechanical irritation of the mucosa.
Raw Material Quality: It is important to choose products made from quality grain, as bran can accumulate pesticides if stored improperly.

whole-grain-pasta.name: Whole Grain Pasta
whole-grain-pasta.description: Whole grain pasta is a nutritionally enriched form of a carbohydrate matrix produced from whole wheat flour, which retains all grain layers: bran, endosperm, and germ. The product is characterized by a high content of complex carbohydrates and dietary fiber, ensuring a physiologically optimal glucose response and prolonged satiety.
whole-grain-pasta.macroIntro: The macronutrient profile provides balanced energy support while maintaining a low glycemic index, promoting the body's metabolic flexibility.
whole-grain-pasta.microIntro: This product is an important source of minerals and B-vitamins involved in energy metabolism and the protection of cellular structures.

healthBenefits: Metabolic Stability: High dietary fiber content helps slow down glucose absorption, preventing hyperglycemia.
Microbiota Support: Prebiotic fibers serve as a substrate for beneficial gut flora, supporting immune system health.
Cardioprotection: Replacing refined carbohydrates with whole grains is associated with a reduced risk of cardiovascular diseases.
Appetite Control: Prolonged digestion and satiety facilitate the control of energy balance and body weight.
whole-grain-pasta.precautionsIntro: Whole grain pasta is a safe product but has limitations:
precautions: Gluten Enteropathy: The product is contraindicated for individuals with diagnosed celiac disease.
Gastroenterological Conditions: During acute gastritis or peptic ulcer disease, coarse fiber may cause mechanical irritation of the mucosa.
Mineral Bioavailability: Phytic acid contained in bran may partially block the absorption of zinc and iron if consumed in excess.
Individual Intolerance: In individuals with heightened sensitivity to wheat components, uncomfortable GI reactions are possible.

beetroot.name: Beetroot
beetroot.description: Beetroot is a highly functional root vegetable possessing a unique profile of bioactive compounds, including betalains (plant pigments) and nitrates. It is an effective natural modulator of cardiovascular function, promoting vasodilation and optimizing energy metabolism in tissues.
beetroot.macroIntro: Beetroot is characterized by moderate caloric content and high sugar levels, which, combined with fiber, ensure a stable energy response.
beetroot.microIntro: The product is a rich source of micronutrients that support metabolic health and the body's detoxification processes.

Detoxification: Betalains stimulate liver function, helping the body effectively neutralize and eliminate toxins.
Digestive Function: Pectin fibers improve intestinal peristalsis and support a healthy microbiota.
Antioxidant Defense: High levels of antioxidants neutralize free radicals, slowing down cellular aging processes.
beetroot.precautionsIntro: Beetroot is a highly beneficial product, but individual characteristics should be considered:
precautions: Oxalates: Beetroot contains oxalates, so individuals prone to forming oxalate kidney stones should limit its consumption.
Hypotension: Due to the vasodilatory effect of nitrates, excessive beetroot consumption can trigger an excessive drop in blood pressure.
Glycemic Control: Beetroot has a moderate glycemic index, so portion control is required in cases of diabetes.
Urine Discoloration: Consuming beetroot can cause temporary urine color changes (beeturia), which is a physiological norm, not a pathology.

radish.name: Radish
radish.description: Radish is a low-calorie root vegetable with pronounced antibacterial and choleretic effects. It is valued for its content of isothiocyanates — sulfur-containing compounds that exhibit antioxidant activity and promote detoxification processes in the body.
radish.macroIntro: Radish has an extremely low energy density, making it an excellent component for low-calorie diets.
radish.microIntro: The product contains important minerals and vitamins that contribute to maintaining metabolic status.

Antimicrobial Effect: Radish components inhibit the growth of pathogenic flora in the GI tract.
Detoxification: Promotes the elimination of excess fluid and the normalization of liver function.
Vascular Support: Helps strengthen vascular walls and normalize cholesterol levels.
radish.precautionsIntro: Radish has an active effect on the GI tract, so moderation is advised:
precautions: GI Disorders: Due to the content of essential oils, radish consumption is not recommended for those with gastritis with high acidity, ulcers, and pancreatitis in the acute stage.
Thyroid Gland: Radish contains goitrogenic substances which, in large amounts, can hinder iodine absorption.
Individual Intolerance: An allergic reaction to components of cruciferous vegetables is possible.

turnip.name: Turnip
turnip.description: The turnip is a dietary root vegetable of the cruciferous family, characterized by high nutrient density and low caloric content. It is a valuable source of vitamin C, fiber, and glucosinolates, which support immune function, metabolic health, and the body's detoxification processes.
turnip.macroIntro: Turnips have low energy value and contribute to prolonged satiety due to significant dietary fiber content.
turnip.microIntro: The product is a biochemically active source of minerals and vitamins working synergistically to maintain systemic homeostasis.

turnip.precautionsIntro: Turnips are beneficial for most people but have certain contraindications:
precautions: GI Conditions: In raw form, turnips can cause flatulence and mucosal irritation, so they are contraindicated during exacerbations of gastritis, ulcers, or pancreatitis.
Endocrine Disorders: In cases of hypothyroidism, consume with caution due to the presence of compounds that can affect iodine absorption.
Individual Intolerance: Allergic reactions characteristic of all members of the cruciferous family are possible.

celery.name: Celery
celery.description: Celery is a low-calorie product with a high concentration of water and bioactive flavonoids (apigenin, luteolin). It is known for its diuretic, anti-inflammatory properties and its ability to support the cardiovascular system due to the presence of phthalides.
celery.macroIntro: Celery has an extremely low energy density, making it an ideal product for adding volume to a diet.
celery.microIntro: The plant is rich in Vitamin K and antioxidants that support vascular elasticity and cellular membrane integrity.

Diuretic Effect: High potassium content and specific essential oils help eliminate excess fluid.
Anti-inflammatory Activity: Luteolin and apigenin suppress markers of systemic inflammation.
Digestive Support: Fiber and high water content prevent constipation and facilitate GI function.
celery.precautionsIntro: Despite all the benefits of celery, several limitations should be considered:
precautions: Allergy: Celery is a common allergen; serious cross-reactions are possible.
Kidney Disease: Due to a mild diuretic effect, moderation should be observed in the presence of serious renal pathologies.
Pregnancy: In very large quantities (concentrated juices, seeds), celery may stimulate uterine contractile activity.

green-onion.name: Green Onion
green-onion.description: Green onion is a valuable nutraceutical product characterized by a high content of phytoncides, vitamins, and antioxidants. It has a pronounced immunomodulatory, antibacterial, and metabolic effect, contributing to the maintenance of the body's homeostasis.
green-onion.macroIntro: It has an extremely low energy value with a high concentration of biologically active substances.
green-onion.microIntro: It is an important source of vitamins K and C, necessary for maintaining vascular tone and immune defense.

Digestion: Contributes to improved appetite and secretion of digestive enzymes.

Hypercoagulation: Due to the high vitamin K content, individuals taking anticoagulants should consult a doctor to control their diet.

eggplant.name: Eggplant
eggplant.description: Eggplant is a low-calorie vegetable of the nightshade family, known for its high content of anthocyanins (nasunin), which have pronounced antioxidant properties. It supports the cardiovascular system, helps control blood sugar levels, and has a mild diuretic effect.
eggplant.macroIntro: Eggplant is characterized by very low energy density and a significant content of dietary fiber, contributing to effective satiety.
eggplant.microIntro: The product is rich in phytonutrients and minerals that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

Oxalates: They contain oxalates, so individuals with kidney stone disease (oxalate type) should exercise moderation.
Individual Intolerance: As a member of the nightshade family, it may cause allergic reactions in predisposed individuals.

hot-pepper.name: Hot Pepper (Chili)
hot-pepper.description: Hot pepper is a vegetable crop containing capsaicin, a unique bioactive compound responsible for its spicy taste, which possesses pronounced metabolic, anti-inflammatory, and analgesic properties.
hot-pepper.macroIntro: It has low calorie content, yet significantly impacts thermogenesis due to its biological activity.
hot-pepper.microIntro: It is a concentrated source of vitamins that support vascular tone and the immune system.

hot-pepper.precautionsIntro: Hot pepper has a powerful physiological effect, so it requires careful handling:

Individual Reaction: May cause severe burning of mucous membranes and skin (use gloves when cooking).
Drug Interaction: May affect the absorption of certain medications.

zucchini.name: Zucchini
zucchini.description: Zucchini is an easily digestible vegetable of the gourd family, possessing high hydration value and containing moderate levels of antioxidants (lutein, zeaxanthin). It serves as a mild diuretic and dietary component that helps normalize water balance.
zucchini.macroIntro: It has very low caloric content and high water content, making it an excellent product for weight management.
zucchini.microIntro: Contains important carotenoids and potassium, supporting eye health and the cardiovascular system.

Dietary Value: High volume with minimal calories contributes to a prolonged feeling of satiety.

precautions: Kidney Conditions: In chronic renal failure, excess potassium in the diet requires medical monitoring.

Raw Consumption: In rare cases, raw zucchini may cause discomfort in people with sensitive stomachs due to the presence of specific proteins (cucurbitacins) in wild varieties, so thermal processing is preferred.

green-peas.name: Green Peas
green-peas.description: Peas are a nutritious member of the legume family, characterized by a high concentration of plant-based protein and dietary fiber. They are a valuable source of complex carbohydrates, B vitamins, and minerals that support muscle mass and stable blood sugar levels.
green-peas.macroIntro: Peas are a nutrient-dense food that provides sustained satiety.
green-peas.microIntro: The product is rich in essential micronutrients that support energy metabolism and the nervous system.

Heart Support: Potassium and magnesium contribute to maintaining normal blood pressure.
Digestive Health: High insoluble fiber content promotes regular bowel movements.
Muscle Support: The combination of protein and complex carbohydrates is beneficial for post-exercise recovery.
green-peas.precautionsIntro: Peas are beneficial but require consideration of individual reactions:
precautions: Flatulence: Like other legumes, peas can cause bloating due to the presence of oligosaccharides (especially when consumed in excess).
Gout: Contains purines, so it is recommended to limit consumption during gout flare-ups.
GI Disorders: During periods of GI disease exacerbation (gastritis, ulcers), peas in rough form may be contraindicated.

beans.name: Beans
beans.description: Beans are a highly nutritious member of the legume family, characterized by a unique combination of plant-based protein, slow-burning carbohydrates, and a high concentration of dietary fiber. They are an important component of diets aimed at maintaining cardiovascular health and glucose control.
beans.macroIntro: Beans have high nutrient density, providing a prolonged sense of satiety due to their complex carbohydrate composition.
beans.microIntro: The product is a powerful source of minerals that support hematopoiesis and energy metabolism.

Energy Value: Complex carbohydrates ensure a stable energy level without spikes.
beans.precautionsIntro: Beans require proper preparation before consumption:
precautions: Anti-nutrients: In their raw state, they contain lectins and phytates that can inhibit nutrient absorption, so soaking and thorough boiling are mandatory.
Flatulence: Can cause bloating due to the presence of complex sugars (oligosaccharides).
Gout: Due to the presence of purines, consumption should be moderate in cases of impaired purine metabolism.

basil.name: Basil
basil.description: Basil is an aromatic herb rich in essential oils (eugenol) and antioxidants. It possesses pronounced anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, and adaptogenic properties, contributing to immune support and the normalization of digestive processes.
basil.macroIntro: It has an extremely low energy value, so it is used in cooking mainly for flavoring.
basil.microIntro: It is an important source of Vitamin K and antioxidants that protect cells from damage.

basil.precautionsIntro: Basil is beneficial, but requires moderation in the following situations:
precautions: Hypercoagulation: Due to the very high Vitamin K content, individuals taking anticoagulant medications (e.g., warfarin) should exercise caution.
Pregnancy: It is not recommended to use in concentrated form (essential oil).
Individual Reaction: Allergies to plants of the Lamiaceae family are possible.

buckwheat.name: Buckwheat
buckwheat.description: Buckwheat is a nutritious food that is technically a pseudocereal (fruit seed) and is gluten-free. It is valued for its high level of antioxidants (rutin), complex carbohydrates, and easily digestible plant proteins.
buckwheat.macroIntro: It has high energy density and a balanced nutrient composition.
buckwheat.microIntro: It is an important source of magnesium, iron, and B vitamins.

Portion Control: Despite its benefits, it is a calorie-dense product; for weight loss, monitoring total intake volume is important.

ginger.name: Ginger
ginger.description: Ginger is an aromatic root containing gingerols and shogaols, which determine its pungent taste and pronounced medicinal properties. It is widely known as an effective anti-nausea remedy and a powerful anti-inflammatory agent.
ginger.macroIntro: Ginger is consumed in small doses as a seasoning, so its calorie count per serving is negligible.
ginger.microIntro: Contains biologically active compounds that have a systemic effect on the body.

Immune Support: Possesses antiseptic and warming properties, useful during colds.

Gallstones: Possesses a pronounced choleretic effect, which may trigger stone movement.

pineapple.name: Pineapple
pineapple.description: Pineapple is a tropical fruit unique for its content of bromelain, a complex of proteolytic enzymes that facilitate protein breakdown and possess anti-inflammatory properties. It is also a rich source of vitamin C and manganese.
pineapple.macroIntro: Pineapple has moderate caloric content and high sugar levels, providing a quick energy response.
pineapple.microIntro: The product contains important trace elements to support immunity and connective tissue health.

tangerine.name: Tangerine
tangerine.description: Tangerine is a citrus fruit rich in vitamin C, flavonoids, and fiber. It has a pronounced antioxidant effect, contributes to immune support, and improves the overall metabolic state of the body.

sour-cream.name: Sour Cream
sour-cream.description: Sour cream is a fermented milk product obtained by fermenting cream with lactic acid bacteria. It is valued for its content of probiotics, fat-soluble vitamins, and calcium, which are necessary for bone tissue and intestinal microflora.
sour-cream.macroIntro: A product with high energy density, consisting mainly of milk fats.
sour-cream.microIntro: It is a source of calcium and B vitamins.

macroNutrients.description: High energy value.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Small amount of milk protein.

microNutrients.description: Beneficial bacteria for intestinal microflora.

healthBenefits: Intestinal Microflora: The presence of lactic acid bacteria helps improve digestion.
Vitamin Absorption: Milk fats help the body absorb fat-soluble vitamins better from other foods.
Bone Health: Contains calcium and vitamin D (in some types) that support bone density.
sour-cream.precautionsIntro: Sour cream is a high-fat product, so consider the following:
precautions: Calorie Control: High fat content requires portion monitoring for weight management.
Cholesterol: Contains saturated fats, which requires caution for cardiovascular conditions.
Lactose: Individuals with severe lactose intolerance should choose lactose-free alternatives.

butter.name: Butter
butter.description: Butter is concentrated milk fat obtained by churning cream. It is an important source of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K2) and conjugated linoleic acid (CLA), which has potential anti-carcinogenic properties.
butter.macroIntro: A product with maximum energy density, consisting almost entirely of lipids.
butter.microIntro: Contains a unique profile of fat-soluble micronutrients.

microNutrients.name: Conjugated Linoleic Acid
microNutrients.description: Fatty acid that supports metabolism.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin K2
microNutrients.description: Promotes proper calcium metabolism in bones.

healthBenefits: Vitamin Source: Provides high bioavailability of vitamins A, D, E, and K2.
Metabolic Support: CLA (in butter from grass-fed cows) may help improve body composition.
Culinary Value: Stable saturated fats make it suitable for many cooking methods at moderate heat.
butter.precautionsIntro: Due to its high energy density and fat composition, moderation is recommended:
precautions: Cardiovascular Risks: High content of saturated fats requires monitoring consumption in cases of dyslipidemia.
Caloric Content: Excessive consumption easily leads to a calorie surplus and weight gain.
Individual Intolerance: Contraindicated for those with a dairy protein (casein) allergy or lactose intolerance (depending on purity).

olive_oil.name: Olive Oil
olive_oil.description: Olive oil (primarily Extra Virgin) is a fundamental component of the Mediterranean diet. It is rich in monounsaturated fatty acids (oleic acid) and powerful polyphenols that provide pronounced antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects.
olive_oil.macroIntro: Pure source of lipids with high energy density.
olive_oil.microIntro: Contains a significant amount of antioxidants and vitamins that protect the cardiovascular system.

macroNutrients.name: Fat
macroNutrients.description: Predominantly monounsaturated fatty acids.

macroNutrients.name: Vitamin E
macroNutrients.description: Powerful fat-soluble antioxidant.

healthBenefits: Cardiovascular Protection: Regular consumption helps lower 'bad' cholesterol and maintain vascular elasticity.
Anti-inflammatory Effect: Contains oleocanthal, which possesses anti-inflammatory properties comparable to some pharmaceutical analgesics.
Antioxidant Profile: Polyphenols neutralize free radicals, slowing down cellular aging.
olive_oil.precautionsIntro: Olive oil is a beneficial product, but consider the following:
precautions: Calorie Control: Due to its extremely high energy density, it is necessary to strictly dose intake when managing weight.
Thermal Processing: Extra Virgin oils have a relatively low smoke point, so it is recommended to use them primarily raw (dressings, sauces) to preserve all biologically active substances.
Storage: Sensitive to light and heat; requires storage in a dark glass container in a cool place to prevent oxidation.

black-tea.name: Black Tea
black-tea.description: Black tea is a product of full fermentation of the tea leaf (Camellia sinensis), rich in polyphenols (theaflavins and thearubigins) and caffeine. It has a pronounced tonic effect, improves cognitive functions, and supports the cardiovascular system when consumed in moderation.
black-tea.macroTitle: Macro Nutrients (per 100 ml of brewed beverage)
black-tea.macroIntro: The beverage contains almost no calories if consumed without additives (sugar, milk).
black-tea.microIntro: A source of antioxidants that support metabolism and cellular protection.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Zero energy density.

macroNutrients.name: Caffeine
macroNutrients.description: Stimulates the central nervous system.

microNutrients.name: Theaflavins
microNutrients.description: Antioxidants unique to black tea.

microNutrients.name: Fluoride
microNutrients.description: Supports dental enamel health.

healthBenefits: Cardioprotection: Flavonoids contribute to improved vascular endothelial function and reduced risk of cardiovascular diseases.
Cognitive Effect: Caffeine combined with L-theanine improves concentration and productivity.
Antioxidant Defense: Theaflavins help neutralize free radicals.
Metabolism: Contributes to increased general body tone.
black-tea.precautionsIntro: Black tea is beneficial but requires moderation:
precautions: Iron Deficiency: Tannins may inhibit the absorption of non-heme iron from plant-based foods when consumed simultaneously.
Sleep: High caffeine content may disrupt sleep phases if consumed in the afternoon.
GI Sensitivity: In some people, it may cause irritation of the stomach lining due to tannins.

green_tea.name: Green Tea
green_tea.description: Green tea is a minimally fermented tea leaf (Camellia sinensis) rich in catechins (especially EGCG). It is known for its pronounced antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, as well as its ability to support metabolism and cognitive functions.
green_tea.macroTitle: Macro Nutrients (per 100 ml of brewed beverage)
green_tea.macroIntro: The beverage contains almost no calories if consumed without additives (sugar, honey).
green_tea.microIntro: It is a concentrated source of polyphenols.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Minimal energy value.

macroNutrients.name: Caffeine
macroNutrients.description: Mild CNS stimulant.

microNutrients.name: Epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG)
microNutrients.description: Powerful antioxidant characteristic of green tea.

microNutrients.name: L-theanine
microNutrients.description: Amino acid that promotes relaxation without drowsiness.

healthBenefits: Antioxidant Defense: Catechins help protect cells from oxidative damage.
Metabolic Support: May contribute to a slight increase in fat oxidation rate.
Cognitive Effect: The combination of caffeine and L-theanine improves focus.
Cardiovascular System: Regular consumption is linked to a reduced risk of heart disease factors.
green_tea.precautionsIntro: Green tea is beneficial but requires caution:
precautions: Iron Absorption: Tannins may decrease iron absorption from plant-based foods.
Caffeine: Despite having less than coffee or black tea, individuals with high sensitivity should limit intake.
Liver: Extremely high dosages of green tea extracts (in supplement form) can be hepatotoxic.

coffee.name: Coffee (Black)
coffee.description: Coffee is a popular beverage obtained from roasted coffee beans. It is a powerful CNS stimulant due to its high caffeine content and contains significant amounts of antioxidants, including chlorogenic acid.
coffee.macroTitle: Macro Nutrients (per 100 ml of brewed beverage)
coffee.macroIntro: Black coffee contains almost no calories if no sugar, cream, or milk is added.
coffee.microIntro: Contains a wide range of bioactive compounds and minerals in trace amounts.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Zero energy density.

macroNutrients.name: Caffeine
macroNutrients.description: Main active component.

microNutrients.name: Chlorogenic Acid
microNutrients.description: Antioxidant that helps regulate metabolism.

microNutrients.name: Potassium
microNutrients.description: Supports cardiovascular system function.

healthBenefits: Cognitive Functions: Caffeine improves concentration, memory, and general productivity.
Physical Activity: Increases endurance and workout efficiency by mobilizing fatty acids.
Metabolism: Chlorogenic acid may help improve insulin sensitivity.
Antioxidant Defense: One of the largest sources of antioxidants in many people's diets.
coffee.precautionsIntro: Coffee is an active product, so it is important to consider:
precautions: Sleep Disruption: Caffeine blocks adenosine receptors, which can cause insomnia if consumed in the afternoon.
Cardiovascular Reaction: Can increase blood pressure and cause tachycardia in sensitive individuals.
GI Impact: Stimulates hydrochloric acid production, which may be undesirable for gastritis or high acidity.
Nutrient Absorption: In large amounts, it may interfere with calcium and iron absorption.

dark-chocolate.name: Dark Chocolate
dark-chocolate.description: Dark chocolate is a processed cocoa bean product rich in flavonoids, theobromine, and antioxidants. With high cocoa content, it acts as a functional food, contributing to improved blood circulation and mood.
dark-chocolate.macroIntro: A product with very high energy density due to its cocoa butter content.
dark-chocolate.microIntro: It is a concentrated source of magnesium, iron, and copper.

Psychological Well-being: Stimulates the production of endorphins and serotonin.
Antioxidant Defense: High polyphenol content fights free radicals.
dark-chocolate.precautionsIntro: Chocolate is a very high-calorie and potent product, so it is important to:
precautions: Portion Control: High energy density requires limiting consumption (15-30g per day is recommended).
Caffeine Content: Consider the total daily caffeine dose if you are sensitive to stimulants.
Oxalates: Contains oxalates, which requires caution if you are prone to kidney stones.

honey.name: Honey
honey.description: Honey is a natural product produced by bees from plant nectar. It is rich in enzymes, antioxidants, and natural sugars, acting as a natural energy booster and antiseptic.
honey.macroIntro: A product with a high concentration of easily digestible carbohydrates.
honey.microIntro: Contains trace amounts of B vitamins, Vitamin C, and minerals.

macroNutrients.description: Primarily composed of fructose and glucose.

microNutrients.description: Natural antioxidants with anti-inflammatory effects.

healthBenefits: Antiseptic effect: Honey possesses significant antibacterial properties.
Immune support: Assists the body in fighting common colds and infections.
Energy source: Quickly replenishes glycogen stores, beneficial for physical exertion.
Soothing effect: A traditional remedy for relieving coughs and improving sleep quality.
honey.precautionsIntro: Honey is a potent allergen and a source of simple sugars, therefore it is important to:
precautions: Allergies: Risk of allergic reactions to bee pollen.
Diabetes: A high glycemic index requires caution for those with metabolic disorders.
Botulism: Honey should never be given to infants under 1 year of age.

olives.name: Olives
olives.description: Olives are the fruit of the olive tree, rich in monounsaturated fatty acids and vitamin E. They are a key component of the Mediterranean diet, known for supporting heart health.
olives.macroIntro: A product high in healthy plant-based fats.
olives.microIntro: An excellent source of vitamin E and polyphenols.

olives.precautionsIntro: Olives undergo a curing process, so it is important to consider:
precautions: Salt: High sodium content due to brining, which requires moderation for those with hypertension.

mung-bean.name: Mung Bean
mung-bean.description: Mung beans are small green beans that possess high nutritional value and excellent digestibility. They are a valuable source of plant-based protein and antioxidants, and are generally easier on the digestive system than many other types of legumes.
mung-bean.macroIntro: Mung beans are characterized by a balanced composition of proteins and complex carbohydrates, providing prolonged satiety.
mung-bean.microIntro: The product is rich in important minerals, including manganese, magnesium, and folic acid.

precautions: Individual Intolerance: Allergic reactions are possible, though rare.
Processing: Like all legumes, they require rinsing and cooking to neutralize natural anti-nutrients.
Dietary Restrictions: If you have severe GI tract conditions in an acute phase, consult with a doctor.

salt.name: Salt
salt.description: Table salt (sodium chloride) is an essential electrolyte that plays a critical role in maintaining fluid balance, nerve conduction, and muscle contraction.
salt.macroIntro: The primary source of sodium and chloride in the human diet.
salt.microIntro: Unrefined varieties may contain trace amounts of other minerals.

macroNutrients.name: Chloride
macroNutrients.description: Essential for the production of gastric acid.

Nervous system: Necessary for the transmission of nerve impulses.
Muscle function: Involved in the processes of muscle contraction and relaxation.
Digestion: Maintains the necessary stomach acidity for protein digestion.
salt.precautionsIntro: Excessive salt intake is associated with health risks:
precautions: Hypertension: Excessive sodium retains water and raises blood pressure.
Edema: High salt intake contributes to fluid retention in body tissues.
Kidneys: High consumption increases the burden on the excretory system.

halva.name: Halva
halva.description: Halva is a traditional Oriental delicacy made from oilseeds (sunflower, sesame) or nuts and a caramel mass. It is a concentrated source of plant-based fats, vitamins, and energy.
halva.macroIntro: A product with very high energy density due to the content of high-quality fats.
halva.microIntro: Rich in Vitamin E, B vitamins, and essential minerals (magnesium, calcium, iron).

Digestibility: Plant fats from seeds are easier for the body to assimilate than animal fats.

precautions: Portion control: High caloric value requires limiting portions (20-30g per day recommended).

Allergies: May cause allergic reactions (especially sesame-based halva).

dates.name: Dates
dates.description: Dates are the fruit of the date palm, known for their high natural sweetness and rich fiber content. They are an excellent natural sugar substitute and a source of quick-acting carbohydrates.
dates.macroIntro: A product with high energy value due to its high natural sugar content.
dates.microIntro: Rich in potassium, copper, and Vitamin B6.

Heart health: Potassium helps normalize blood pressure.
Natural sweetness: A healthy alternative to confectionery with added sugars.

Diabetes: They have a high glycemic index, requiring blood sugar monitoring.

prunes.name: Prunes
prunes.description: Prunes are dried plums renowned for their exceptional contributions to digestive health and skeletal integrity. Packed with concentrated dietary fiber, essential minerals like potassium, and vital bone-protecting vitamins, they serve as a potent, natural source of sustained energetic vitality.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Energy provided by the food to fuel your body's daily metabolic processes and physical activities.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Provides modest amounts of plant-based amino acids, aiding in basic cellular maintenance and muscle retention.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: Extremely low fat content, consisting primarily of trace, healthy unsaturated fatty acids.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: A dense source of complex carbohydrates, natural fruit sugars (fructose and glucose), and unique sugar alcohols.

microNutrients.name: Dietary Fiber
microNutrients.description: Crucial for optimal digestive regulation. Promotes gut motility, feeds beneficial microbiome strains, and slows glucose absorption.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin K
microNutrients.description: An absolute powerhouse for bone density. Plays an indispensable role in activating proteins required for bone mineralization and optimal blood clotting function.

microNutrients.name: Potassium
microNutrients.description: A critical electrolyte that helps manage fluid balance, regulates heart rhythm, stabilizes blood pressure, and reduces stroke vulnerability.

microNutrients.name: Copper
microNutrients.description: Essential micro-mineral that supports iron absorption, aids in red blood cell generation, and sustains healthy connective tissues.

microNutrients.name: Manganese
microNutrients.description: Contributes significantly to bone matrix formation, carbohydrate metabolism, and active free-radical defense systems.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B6
microNutrients.description: Supports neurotransmitter production, cognitive focus, and effective energy conversion from consumed macronutrients.

microNutrients.name: Magnesium
microNutrients.description: Assists with over 300 biochemical pathways, including physical muscle relaxation, nerve signal transmissions, and cellular ATP energy synthesis.

healthBenefits: Exceptional Digestive Support: Prunes work naturally to relieve constipation due to their high fiber content paired with 14.7g of sorbitol—a sugar alcohol that draws moisture into the large intestine to smooth stool transit.

Preserves & Enhances Bone Density: Regular prune intake has been clinically demonstrated to prevent bone mineral loss and significantly decrease the structural risks of osteoporosis, primarily due to synergistic blends of Vitamin K, potassium, and boron.
High Antioxidant Shielding: Loaded with polyphenolic compounds, prunes effectively neutralize oxidative free radicals, helping to stifle chronic inflammation throughout the cardiovascular network.

Aids Satiety & Weight Regulation: Despite their rich sweetness, the high concentration of dietary fibers creates a lower glycemic impact, delaying hunger cues and helping stabilize blood sugar patterns.

Cardiovascular Protection: The rich reservoir of bioavailable potassium coupled with protective fiber targets the minimization of artery-hardening factors and helps keep blood pressure reading ranges optimal.
prunes.precautionsIntro: Sorbitol Sensitivity: The presence of natural sorbitol can cause mild gastrointestinal distress, bloating, or loose stools if prunes are consumed excessively within a short timeframe. Introduce them gradually into your diet to assess tolerance.
precautions: Acrylamide Concentration: Because they undergo a heat-based drying process, prunes contain trace amounts of acrylamide. While these levels are well within safe thresholds for human ingestion, moderate culinary consumption remains recommended.

Caloric Density Considerations: As with all dehydrated fruits, water removal intensifies sugar and caloric concentrations. Portion tracking is essential if managing precise weight loss or rigid diabetic nutritional frameworks.

Sulfur Dioxide Preservation: Certain commercially packed prunes utilize sulfites to retain texture and stave off spoilage. Individuals with documented sulfite hypersensitivities or asthma should carefully seek out 'organic' or 'sulfite-free' variations.

black-cumin.name: Black Cumin
black-cumin.description: Black seed (Nigella sativa) is a legendary medicinal spice traditionally known as the 'seed of blessing.' It is highly revered in modern nutrition for its exceptional concentrations of thymoquinone, powerful volatile oils, and essential fatty acids that support robust immune architecture.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Energy provided by the food to fuel your body's daily metabolic processes and physical activities.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: Rich in healthy polyunsaturated and monounsaturated fatty acids, notably linoleic acid (Omega-6) and oleic acid (Omega-9).

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Mainly composed of complex carbohydrates and a substantial matrix of non-digestible dietary fibers.

microNutrients.name: Dietary Fiber
microNutrients.description: An extraordinarily dense source of fiber that facilitates excellent gastrointestinal transit and acts as a robust prebiotic.

microNutrients.name: Iron
microNutrients.description: Exceeds the daily value milestone. Crucial for red blood cell formation, cellular oxygenation, and preventing fatigue.

microNutrients.name: Calcium
microNutrients.description: Vital for maintaining skeletal bone density, optimizing muscle contractions, and managing nerve signal transmissions.

microNutrients.name: Zinc
microNutrients.description: An indispensable mineral for reinforcing immune cell defenses, accelerating wound healing, and supporting DNA synthesis.

microNutrients.name: Magnesium
microNutrients.description: Supports cellular energy ATP manufacturing, calms nervous system hyper-excitability, and regulates muscle health.

microNutrients.name: Thymoquinone
microNutrients.description: The star bioactive phytochemical in black seed. Possesses intense antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and hepatoprotective properties.

healthBenefits: Potent Immune System Modulator: Thymoquinone directly stimulates the activity of natural killer (NK) cells and macrophages, optimizing the body's baseline resistance against viral and bacterial threats.

Powerful Bronchodilator & Respiratory Support: Historically used for asthma and allergies. Its volatile oils exert a calming, anti-inflammatory effect on lung tissues, helping to relax bronchial smooth muscles.
Supports Blood Sugar Regulation: Clinical trials indicate that black seed assists in improving fasting blood glucose, reducing insulin resistance, and protecting pancreatic beta-cell functionality.
Enhances Cardiovascular & Lipid Profiles: Helps decrease 'bad' LDL cholesterol and plasma triglycerides, contributing to cleaner arterial passage and optimal systemic blood pressure support.

Robust Gastrointestinal Protection: The seed oil exhibits noticeable anti-ulcer actions, shielding the gastric mucosa from damage, suppressing harmful bacteria like H. pylori, and mitigating severe bloating.
black-cumin.precautionsIntro: Dosage and Concentrates: While black seeds are highly safe in standard culinary amounts, therapeutic concentrations (like pure black seed oil) are highly potent. Overconsumption can strain liver or kidney processing pathways.
precautions: Pregnancy Warnings: Large medicinal doses of black seed are contraindicated during pregnancy as it can alter or stimulate uterine smooth muscle contractions.
Bleeding & Surgery Risks: Black seed can naturally slow down blood clotting mechanics. Discontinue therapeutic use at least two weeks prior to any scheduled surgical or dental procedures.

Hypoglycemia Interventions: Due to its natural capacity to drive blood sugar downward, individuals taking prescription antidiabetic medications must track glucose closely to avert sudden hypoglycemic drops.

turkey.name: Turkey
turkey.description: Turkey is an exceptional, lean whole-food protein source highly favored in sports and therapeutic nutrition. It stands out for its remarkably low saturated fat content, high bioavailability of essential amino acids, and rich concentration of mood-regulating tryptophan.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Energy provided by the food to fuel your body's daily metabolic processes and physical activities.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: An incredibly dense source of complete, high-quality protein containing all essential amino acids necessary for optimal muscle retention and repair.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: Extremely lean when skinless, keeping saturated fat to an absolute minimum while offering trace essential lipids.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Completely free of carbohydrates, making it ideal for blood sugar stabilization and low-glycemic or ketogenic dietary goals.

microNutrients.name: Selenium
microNutrients.description: A potent trace mineral and antioxidant that critical for activating thyroid hormones and neutralizing oxidative damage.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B3 (Niacin)
microNutrients.description: Essential for converting macronutrients into functional ATP cellular energy and maintaining skin integrity and nervous system health.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B6
microNutrients.description: Vital for neurotransmitter synthesis, cognitive cognitive function, and healthy red blood cell production.

microNutrients.name: Zinc
microNutrients.description: Supports immune cellular defense mechanisms, accelerates wound healing, and plays a foundational role in DNA synthesis.

microNutrients.name: Phosphorus
microNutrients.description: Works closely with calcium to build and support structural skeletal bone density and tooth enamel strength.

microNutrients.name: Tryptophan
microNutrients.description: An essential amino acid used by the brain to manufacture serotonin (the 'happy' neurotransmitter) and melatonin, promoting better sleep architectures.

healthBenefits: Accelerates Muscle Development & Fat Loss: Offering over 30g of protein per serving with almost zero fat, turkey induces high satiety levels, boosts thermogenesis, and optimally fuels lean muscle recovery.

Enhances Mood and Sleep Architecture: The rich reservoir of tryptophan, when combined with healthy dietary carbs in a meal, smoothly crosses the blood-brain barrier to synthesize serotonin, helping alleviate stress and improve sleep quality.
Supports Thyroid Optimization: High natural levels of selenium and zinc protect the thyroid gland from oxidative stress and aid the smooth conversion of thyroid hormones into their active forms.

Reinforces Cardiovascular Integrity: Due to its negligible saturated fat and sodium levels (when unprocessed), turkey breast fits perfectly into heart-healthy, low-cholesterol dietary strategies to maintain blood pressure profiles.
Combats Chronic Fatigue: The powerhouse combination of B-vitamins (B3 and B6) works aggressively within cellular pathways to streamline metabolic energy extraction from your daily food intake.
turkey.precautionsIntro: Sodium and Processing Hazards: While fresh, whole turkey breast is incredibly healthy, commercially processed alternatives like turkey deli meats, ham, or bacon are highly loaded with added sodium, nitrates, and chemical preservatives.
precautions: High Purine Concentration: Turkey contains moderate-to-high levels of purines, which break down into uric acid. Individuals managing gout or prone to uric acid kidney stones should monitor their total portion consumption.

Hidden Allergens in Pre-Basted Birds: Many commercially frozen whole turkeys are injected with artificial brines, flavor enhancers, or hidden gluten to retain moisture. Always read packaging labels closely if you have celiac disease or food sensitivities.

Proper Internal Cooking Safeguards: Like all poultry, turkey carries risk of Campylobacter or Salmonella colonization. Always cook turkey until it reaches a safe internal target temperature of 74°C (165°F) to eliminate bacterial hazards.

hazelnut.name: Hazelnut
hazelnut.description: Hazelnut (filbert) is a nutrient-dense whole food celebrated for its exceptional brain-boosting capabilities and cardioprotective properties. Rich in monounsaturated fats, powerful vitamin E antioxidants, and structural minerals, it serves as an elite fuel source for metabolic longevity.

precautions: Phytic Acid Mineral Binding: Unfortified soy milk contains noticeable baselines of **phytic acid**. This plant antinutrient can bind to divalent minerals like calcium, zinc, and iron within the digestive tract, slightly reducing their total bioavailable absorption fields.

Severe Immunological Soy Allergies: Soybeans contain highly reactive storage proteins (such as Gly m 4). Individuals diagnosed with a confirmed **soy allergy** can experience rapid systemic immune responses, ranging from hives and oral itching to severe anaphylactic constraints.

Goitrogenic Thyroid Interferences: Massive, unmonitored consumption of concentrated soy compounds may interfere with **iodine absorption** and thyroid hormone synthesis. Individuals dealing with untreated hypothyroidism or severe iodine deficiency should balance their daily intake limits.

soy-sauce.name: Soy Sauce
soy-sauce.imageAlt: deep translucent dark amber soy sauce pooling elegantly in a small minimalist ceramic dipping bowl
soy-sauce.description: Soy sauce is a deeply fermented liquid condiment traditionally produced by fermenting a combined matrix of soybeans (Glycine max), cracked roasted wheat, water, and sodium chloride using specialized fungal cultures (Aspergillus oryzae or Aspergillus sojae). Over a prolonged aging window lasting months to years, complex microbial proteolysis splits dense plant globulin proteins into a dense array of free organic amino acids—most notably glutamic acid—while yeasts convert sugars into short-chain organic acids and complex aromatic esters. Operating within human culinary physiology, this highly concentrated dark amber extract acts as a profound gustatory stimulator, maximizing the expression of the savory (umami) receptor network and accelerating digestive proteolytic enzyme secretions.
soy-sauce.macroIntro: Soy sauce presents an intensely low-lipid fluid macro framework strictly dominated by hydrolyzed plant peptides and a high, concentrated mineral-saline baseline.
soy-sauce.microIntro: The dark aged condiment concentrates an exceptional volume of free amino acids, active organic fermentation acids, and a substantial, clinically significant sodium payload.

macroNutrients.name: Protein

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Derived primarily from the enzymatic breakdown of wheat starches, consisting of simple sugars that are largely consumed by active yeasts to form complex flavor compounds.

microNutrients.name: Sodium
microNutrients.description: An exceptionally high concentration of essential extracellular electrolyte used as a natural preservative, deeply impacting systemic osmotic fluid pressure structures.

microNutrients.name: Free Glutamic Acid
microNutrients.description: A naturally occurring non-essential amino acid that directly binds to peripheral T1R1/T1R3 tongue receptors, generating the rich organoleptic umami response.

microNutrients.name: Manganese
microNutrients.description: An active structural trace mineral cofactor that helps drive internal protein metabolism, connective tissue repair, and free radical defense mechanisms.

microNutrients.name: Iron

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B3 (Niacin)
microNutrients.description: A crucial water-soluble cofactor synthesized during grain fermentation that optimizes metabolic cellular respiration and protects mucosal tissue integrity.

healthBenefits: Profound Umami Receptor Activation: Concentrated payloads of natural **free glutamic acid** engage savory taste receptors, instantly maximizing meal palatability and stimulating immediate salivary flow.

Gastric and Digestive Secretion Induction: The specific combination of organic fermentation acids and peptides signals the stomach to increase hydrochloric acid and pepsin output, improving overall digestive efficiency.

Bioaccessible Plant Peptide Assimilation: Prolonged microbial aging pre-digests dense legume proteins, supplying the jejunum with **instantly absorbable amino acids** requiring zero digestive energy expenditure.

Salt-Reduction Culinary Utility: Due to its highly concentrated, deeply savory taste profile, a minimal splash of soy sauce can replace much larger quantities of standard table salt, lowering net sodium usage.

Antioxidant Fermentation Compounds: Unique dark melanoidin compounds generated during the aging process exhibit noticeble free-radical scavenging capabilities, shielding gastrointestinal tissues from local oxidation.
soy-sauce.precautionsIntro: Severe Sodium Fluid Volume Strains, True Gluten/Soy Immunological Flares, and Biogenic Amine/Histamine Sensitivities: Conscious portioning protects cardiovascular and vascular tone.
precautions: Extreme Sodium and Fluid Volume Load: Carrying an immense **~5493mg of sodium per 100g**, soy sauce demands strict portion control. Excessive use can cause rapid extracellular fluid retention, inducing sudden blood pressure elevations and placing acute stress on compromised renal or cardiac architectures.

Biogenic Amine and Histamine Reactivity: The lengthy natural fermentation process generates noticeable volumes of **histamine and tyramine**. Individuals suffering from Histamine Intolerance ($HIT$) or those taking monoamine oxidase inhibitors ($MAOIs$) may experience rapid headaches, flushing, or gastrointestinal distress.

Latent Gluten and Soy Allergenic Risks: Traditionally brewed varieties contain both **soybeans and wheat structural proteins**. While fermentation alters many peptide chains, individuals diagnosed with severe celiac disease, wheat allergies, or true soy hypersensitivity must exercise extreme caution or choose specialized gluten-free alternatives (such as Tamari).
